svg.title: LMU with DLSS through NVIDIA’s NGX
svg.text: LMU with DLSS through NVIDIA’s NGX
Experimental (lmu_dlss). LMU ships no DLSS; Sim-QVFR calls NGX on LMU’s own device, on top of the multi-view path. Every input
comes from the OpenXR and D3D11 calls LMU makes anyway and two more matrix reads. LMU’s code isn’t changed, hooked or called.

svg.text: Violet marks what DLSS adds to the multi-view path (LMU-MVR-ARCHITECTURE.svg); the rest is as there. Still no arrow points into LMU’s code:
the jitter reaches LMU through the FOV it asks for, and DLSS runs between LMU’s own D3D11 calls. Needs multi_view=1; lmu_dlss=0 by default.
Known limits: the motion vectors come from depth, so other cars smear; a focus view drawn smaller picks its texture mips for that size (no per-view
mip bias at the API level). The VR UI’s canvas with mips (lmu_ui_mips) is on with or without DLSS. Design as of 2026-11-10, branch lmu-dlss.
